text: Meanwhile Saul, still breathing threats and murder against the disciples of the Lord, went to the high priest
and asked him for letters to the synagogues in Damascus, so that if he found anyone belonging to the Way, men or women, he could bring them back to Jerusalem in chains.
As he traveled and was approaching Damascus, suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him.
He fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to him, "Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?"
"Who are you, Lord?" he asked. "I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting," he replied.
"Now get up and go into the city, and you will be told what you must do."
The men traveling with him stood speechless; they heard the voice but saw no one.
Saul got up from the ground, and though his eyes were open he could see nothing. So they took him by the hand and led him into Damascus.
For three days he was without sight, and he neither ate nor drank.
In Damascus there was a disciple named Ananias. The Lord said to him in a vision, "Ananias!" "Here I am, Lord," he answered.
The Lord said to him, "Get up and go to the street called Straight, and ask at the house of Judas for a man from Tarsus named Saul. He is praying,
and in a vision he has seen a man named Ananias come in and lay his hands on him so that he may see again."
But Ananias answered, "Lord, I have heard from many people about this man and all the harm he has done to your saints in Jerusalem.
And here he has authority from the chief priests to arrest everyone who calls on your name."
But the Lord said to him, "Go, for this man is my chosen instrument to carry my name before the Gentiles and their kings and before the people of Israel.
I myself will show him how much he must suffer for my name."

So Ananias went and entered the house. He laid his hands on Saul and said, "Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus, who appeared to you on the road as you were coming, has sent me so that you may see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit."
Immediately something like scales fell from his eyes, and he could see again. He got up and was baptized,
and after taking some food he regained his strength. He stayed some days with the disciples in Damascus,
and at once he began to proclaim Jesus in the synagogues: "He is the Son of God."
All who heard him were astounded and said, "Isn't this the man who wreaked havoc in Jerusalem among those who call on this name? And hasn't he come here to bring them in chains to the chief priests?"
But Saul grew all the stronger and confounded the Jews living in Damascus by proving that Jesus is the Christ.
After many days had passed, the Jews plotted to kill him,
but Saul learned of their plot. They were watching the gates day and night in order to kill him,
so his disciples took him by night and lowered him in a basket through the wall.

versions.text: so his disciples took him by night and lowered him through an opening in the wall in a basket.
versions.explanation: "an opening in" adds words not in the Greek, and the double "in" construction ("in the wall in a basket") is awkward when read aloud.

text: When he came to Jerusalem, he tried to join the disciples, but they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.

But Barnabas took him and brought him to the apostles. He told them how Saul had seen the Lord on the road, that the Lord had spoken to him, and how in Damascus he had preached boldly in the name of Jesus.
So he went in and out among them in Jerusalem, speaking boldly in the name of the Lord.

versions.text: So he moved about freely among them in Jerusalem, speaking boldly in the name of the Lord.
versions.explanation: The Greek idiom "coming in and going out" describes ordinary fellowship and movement among the believers; "moved about freely" blurs it with the following "boldly" (παρρησιαζόμενος) and slightly duplicates the sense of freedom.

text: He talked and debated with the Greek-speaking Jews, but they tried to kill him.

versions.text: He talked and debated with the Greek-speaking Jews, but they set out to kill him.
versions.explanation: ἐπεχείρουν is an imperfect expressing repeated attempt; "tried to kill him" is more accurate and reads more smoothly aloud than "set out to kill him."

text: When the brothers found out, they took him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.
So the church throughout Judea, Galilee, and Samaria had peace and was built up. Living in the fear of the Lord and in the encouragement of the Holy Spirit, it continued to grow.
As Peter traveled about the country, he also came down to the saints living in Lydda.
There he found a man named Aeneas, who had been bedridden for eight years, paralyzed.
Peter said to him, "Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and make your bed." And immediately he got up.
All who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw him, and they turned to the Lord.
In Joppa there was a disciple named Tabitha, which translated means Dorcas. She was always doing good works and giving to those in need.
About that time she fell sick and died. They washed her body and laid her in an upstairs room.
Since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples heard that Peter was there and sent two men to him with the plea, "Please come to us at once!"

So Peter got up and went with them. When he arrived, they took him to the upstairs room, and all the widows stood around him weeping and showing him the robes and other clothing that Dorcas had made while she was with them.
Peter sent them all out of the room, knelt down, and prayed. Then he turned to the body and said, "Tabitha, get up." She opened her eyes, and when she saw Peter she sat up.
He gave her his hand and helped her to her feet. Then he called the saints and the widows and presented her to them alive.
This became known all over Joppa, and many believed in the Lord.
Peter stayed on in Joppa for many days with a tanner named Simon.

versions.text: Peter stayed in Joppa for some time with a tanner named Simon.
versions.explanation: ἡμέρας ἱκανάς denotes a considerable number of days; "for some time" is vaguer than the Greek. "Stayed on" also captures the sense of remaining after the events just narrated and reads well aloud.
